basic_info: 66-year-old male with chief complaint of constant left shoulder and left elbow pain for five months
present_illness: Onset five months ago following a fall, pain severity variable, impact on physical activity (e.g., gym, weightlifting). The pain is more of a constant ache, but it can get sharper sometimes, especially when moving the arm certain ways. It does not feel like it is swelling or red, and there is no tingling or numbness. It is mostly in the shoulder and elbow, and it does not really go anywhere else. It is just been really persistent. The pain gets worse when lifting things, especially weights at the gym. Range of motion is limited, especially when raising the arm overhead or twisting it. No weakness noted. The patient reports no clicking, popping, or locking sensations in the left shoulder or elbow during movement. The patient has not experienced any recent changes in the pattern or intensity of the pain, nor any new symptoms such as weakness, swelling, or tingling in the left arm or hand.
past_history: The patient fell five months ago while walking on icy stairs, landing on his left side, which likely caused the initial injury to his left shoulder and wrist. No prior history of similar symptoms, surgeries, or conditions reported. No previous shoulder or elbow injuries, surgeries, or conditions reported.
physical_exam: Pain localized to the left shoulder and elbow, with exacerbation during certain arm movements. No swelling, redness, tingling, or numbness. No neurological deficits reported. Range of motion is limited, especially when raising the arm overhead or twisting it.
aux_exam: No imaging studies or specialist consultations have been performed yet.
